# Annotated vision fixtures

This directory contains the hermetic release-gating point-tracking evidence. Evaluation performs no network request, video decode, optional cache lookup, or missing-data skip. Manifest v9 pins the complete upstream video and annotation archives independently and every derived file by exact byte length and SHA-256 before bounded decoding. Its sole frame encoding is lossless `rgb24-xor-delta-gzip`: frame zero is RGB24 and each later frame is the bytewise XOR delta against the preceding decoded frame. The evaluator reconstructs the exact raw payload in place after bounded gzip expansion.

## TAP-Vid RGB-Stacking sample 34

Google DeepMind publishes the [TAP-Vid RGB-Stacking videos and annotations](https://github.com/google-deepmind/tapnet/blob/main/tapnet/tapvid/README.md) under [CC-BY-4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/legalcode). The source archive is `tapvid_rgb_stacking.zip`, 187,291,581 bytes, SHA-256 `ba0cec640deb65ab510bc3920cdaf8b7a2e756fce9fb339199c557ade436b0cc`.

The fixture preserves all 250 decoded 256×256 RGB24 frames from sample `34` in source order and all 30 normalized trajectories and occlusion labels. Manifest v9 records this as an identity derivation from the 256×256 source raster. The primary tracks are `1`, `12`, and `16`; annotation-ranked occlusion-stress tracks are `6`, `9`, and `18`. Each query owns independent spatial, visibility, recovery, outage, and fragmentation limits. The lossless delta frame payload is 2,077,741 bytes with SHA-256 `850207181f01cb06a1b35448ce003dc368ac387b4bac286ac79c8ecdfa3e1283`.

## TAP-Vid-DAVIS `shooting`

The source is DeepMind's `tapvid_davis.zip`, 1,668,710,491 bytes, SHA-256 `60eb6239c57a9877900c269d14637c2b6eece8fa280f59e4592324c6392031b6`. Its internal `SOURCES.md` maps `shooting` to Blender Foundation's [*Tears of Steel* project](https://mango.blender.org/about/). The film is CC-BY-3.0; DeepMind's TAP-Vid-DAVIS point annotations are separately CC-BY-4.0. The manifest records and the license gate validates both components instead of assigning one inaccurate fixture-wide license.

The upstream sample contains 40 RGB frames at 1152×480, 25 normalized point tracks, and visibility labels. Frames were resized to the official TAP-Vid 256×256 evaluation raster with the same per-channel Pillow Lanczos path used by `mediapy.resize_video`, serialized as RGB24 in source order, and losslessly delta-compressed. Manifest v9 machine-validates the 1152×480 source raster, the resize operation, and the exact resampler against the 256×256 derived raster; an identity declaration or ambiguous resampler is rejected. The pinned cadence is the source film's 24 FPS, not the 5 FPS visualization encoding published on the dataset page. The derived frame payload is 7,206,138 bytes with SHA-256 `7915cc07515395d091b54aa6955564bba10b3762b8b462c16b2cd16a530cd1ee`; annotations are 30,861 bytes with SHA-256 `18ce8c7553546492bd16de220b295b4c3388ca71b33255d8baca23c200146990`.

Query selection was registered from annotations before HOL replay. Real-world motion tracks `7`, `0`, and `2` cover an always-visible trajectory plus two high-motion short-occlusion reappearances. Terminal-occlusion stress tracks `1`, `9`, and `15` cover 16-, 10-, and 27-frame terminal losses with distinct motion and visibility profiles. Initially ranked repeated/long-reappearance tracks `3`, `5`, and `17` produced no nonzero re-detection regression surface and were rejected rather than admitted with vacuous zero floors. The retained tracks all own positive spatial floors, while recovery fields exist only when the annotation makes that metric applicable.

Weak real-world templates exposed a runtime state defect: a usable but weak tap could enter `degraded`, fail its first LK update, and become permanently `lost` before progressive bootstrap could gather evidence. A first-update failure with bounded tap support now returns to `candidate` without claiming visibility; subsequent bootstrap remains subject to the same query-owned spatial, false-visible, missed-visible, and fragmentation gates. Established RGB-Stacking metrics remain unchanged.

## Perception Test `video_5032`

Google DeepMind publishes the [Perception Test point-tracking data](https://github.com/google-deepmind/perception_test/blob/main/README.md) under [CC-BY-4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/legalcode). The video archive is 417,761,668 bytes with SHA-256 `ae2e9f055d14d9a7773b4ed5ced39e3986a21c4544a21d3d6f13216536211ae3`; the separate annotation archive is 4,888,108 bytes with SHA-256 `c8323aecac91f3ee82f64316b401b027d7b5ea9315cc704b6f47dcc4423f4fdf`. Manifest v9 rejects the former singular source shape, so neither archive can silently stand in for the other.

The fixture retains all 333 source frames at 30 FPS from the 1280×720 fixed-camera sample. Frames use the pinned Pillow Lanczos path to reach the 256×256 evaluation raster; the exact lossless delta payload is 32,183,309 bytes with SHA-256 `22b22291f7b2f3df98ebeaacc78adc2067dfabe8ebe21e61b17feb4943795deb`. All 45 sparse tracks are normalized into the executable first-visible-query contract; source `[y, x]` series become explicit per-frame `[x, y]` pairs and unannotated frames become occluded. The canonical formatted 814,265-byte annotation file has SHA-256 `30e3ec42c0814544ba14761e01b9c94686d2934587f3c6d70795be0047d388a3`.

Query selection was registered from annotation motion and visibility structure before HOL replay. Object-motion tracks `5`, `3`, and `39` cover an always-visible moving point, a short disappearance, and a small ring with repeated long disappearance. Occlusion-stress tracks `0`, `4`, and `35` cover record-length gaps of 207, 86, and 154 frames. Annotation-ranked tracks `41`, `40`, `28`, and `29` produced zero re-detection AJ in replay and were rejected rather than admitted with vacuous floors. The retained 333-frame domain owns positive per-query floors and exposes up to 5,133 ms false visibility, 4,467 ms missed visibility, 900 ms stable recovery latency, and six acquired-track fragmentations. Its six-query aggregate is AJ `0.25433557684855157`, threshold accuracy `0.3987086359967716`, occlusion accuracy `0.6075749605470805`, re-detection AJ `0.07826449495397754`, and stable recovery 3/6.

These files are outside `src/` and `public/`, so Vite cannot include them in the production application. Do not replace or regenerate them without updating source pins, component provenance, transformations, query rationale, and regression contracts together.
